A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Group|group]] and $N \subseteq M$ [[Definition:Normal Subgroup|normal subgroups]] of $G$.
Then:
:$\paren {G / N} / \paren {M / N} \cong G / M$

B_source.statement: Collapsing a set first by an [[Definition:Equivalence Relation|equivalence]] $\sim_1$ and then by a coarser equivalence $\sim_2$ has the same effect as collapsing once by $\sim_2$.

substitutions.the two-stage collapse: quotienting first by N and then by the image of M

derived.the composite of the two quotient maps: the single quotient map onto G modulo M
derived.the kernel of the composite: M, so the two-stage quotient is the one-stage quotient

object_map.reformulation: Replace two successive collapses by the single collapse their composite induces.

validity_conditions: The image of M in G modulo N is normal there, so the second quotient is defined; this needs M normal in G, not merely in N.
The composite of the two quotient maps is surjective, being a composite of surjections.
Its kernel is exactly M, since an element maps to the identity precisely when its class modulo N lies in the image of M.
proof_plan:
Form $G / N$.
The image of $M$ there is $M / N$, which is normal in $G / N$.

Compose the [[Definition:Quotient Epimorphism|quotient maps]]:
:$G \to G / N \to \paren {G / N} / \paren {M / N}$
The composite $\phi$ is a [[Definition:Surjection|surjection]].

We have:
:$g \in \map \ker \phi \iff g N \in M / N \iff g \in M$
so $\map \ker \phi = M$.

By the [[First Isomorphism Theorem for Groups]]:
:$G / M \cong \paren {G / N} / \paren {M / N}$
which is the [[Third Isomorphism Theorem for Groups]].
{{qed}}
